name: ECOLI70
description:
The columns in this dataset (e.g., "aceB", "asnA", etc.) are likely gene names or protein identifiers from the E. coli genome. These represent features (predictor variables) in our dataset. However, without additional context (e.g., metadata or documentation), we can't definitively say what each column represents.

From the library bnlearn, we used the next code in R (to reproduce https://openreview.net/pdf?id=fPVRcJqspu):


install.packages("bnlearn"); 
library(bnlearn)
data(package="bnlearn")


# Load the RDA file (this creates an object named 'bn' in your environment)
load("ECOLI70.rda")  # Replace with your actual file path

# Rename the object for clarity
ecoli_bn <- bn


# Load the RDS file directly
ecoli_bn <- readRDS("ECOLI70.rds")  # Replace with your actual file path


# Generate 1000 synthetic observations from the network
ecoli_data <- rbn(ecoli_bn, n = 2000)

# Save as CSV
write.csv(ecoli_data, "ECOLI70_synthetic_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)


For this dataset we decided to define the target variable as "aceB". This is an arbitrary choice, and you may want to explore other columns as the target variable. The target variable is the variable that you want to predict in your machine learning model.
creator: Schafer, Juliane and Strimmer, Korbinian
citation: Schafer, Juliane and Strimmer, Korbinian. "A Shrinkage Approach to Large-Scale Covariance Matrix Estimation and Implications for Functional Genomics" Statistical Applications in Genetics and Molecular Biology, vol. 4, no. 1, 2005. https://doi.org/10.2202/1544-6115.1175"
